name: Oral semaglutide (Rybelsus)
lead: Oral semaglutide, sold as Rybelsus, is a tablet form of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide. It was the first GLP-1 receptor agonist developed for oral administration, co-formulated with an absorption enhancer, sodium N-(8-[2-hydroxybenzoyl] amino) caprylate, that helps the peptide survive the stomach.[1]

Rybelsus was approved in the US in September 2019 and in the EU in April 2020 for type 2 diabetes; in December 2025 the FDA approved an oral semaglutide for weight management under the Wegovy brand.[2] Its use for weight loss in people without diabetes is discussed in appearance and fat-loss communities, where the pill is sometimes regarded as an alternative to injections.

paras: Rybelsus is indicated as an add-on therapy for adults with type 2 diabetes,[1] and a January 2023 label update allowed first-line use.[2] In October 2025 the FDA expanded its indication to reducing the risk of major cardiovascular events in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes.[2]

Reviews of the pharmacology and clinical programme describe improvements in glycaemic control and body weight in people with type 2 diabetes.[1][3][4] A registered phase 4 trial has examined oral semaglutide for overweight or obesity.[5]

The most common effects of semaglutide are nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation and abdominal pain. The US label carries a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumours, and semaglutide is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.[2] A case report described reversible bilateral central scotoma associated with oral semaglutide.[6]

Oral semaglutide has 94% homology with human GLP-1.[1] Because bioavailability by mouth is low compared with the injection (roughly 1 to 2% versus about 89%), the tablet is formulated with an absorption enhancer.[2][1]
Registered trials examine oral semaglutide in bone turnover, atherosclerosis, Alzheimer's disease, alcohol use disorder and other conditions.[7][8][9][10]

Clinical development has included early-phase trials and phase 3 programmes in type 2 diabetes, summarised in several reviews.[1][3][11] A small retrospective study examined oral semaglutide in diabetic kidney disease.[12]

timeline.event: FDA approves oral semaglutide for weight management (Wegovy) and a cardiovascular indication for Rybelsus.[2]

card.summary: Semaglutide as a daily tablet: proven for type 2 diabetes, with a weight-loss version now approved.
card.note: Boxed thyroid C-cell tumour warning; prescription-only.

quick.overview:
Oral semaglutide is the pill version of the GLP-1 drug semaglutide, sold as Rybelsus for type 2 diabetes. An oral version for weight management was approved in the US in December 2025 under the Wegovy name.

Absorption by mouth is low, so it is combined with an absorption enhancer.
quick.mechanism: It activates GLP-1 receptors, affecting appetite and blood sugar. The tablet formulation includes an enhancer that helps absorption in the stomach.
quick.risks: Common effects are nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation. The label carries a boxed thyroid C-cell tumour warning, and it is contraindicated with certain thyroid cancer histories.
